name: TB-500
summary: A synthetic 7-amino-acid fragment of thymosin beta-4, promoted for injury and wound recovery; FDA found no studies of it in people.
what_it_is: TB-500 is a synthetic seven-amino-acid peptide (acetylated LKKTETQ) that copies amino acids 17 to 23 of thymosin beta-4, a protein found in most cells and in blood, saliva, tears and wound fluid. That stretch of thymosin beta-4 has been linked to wound repair and new blood vessel growth in lab and animal work. FDA stresses that TB-500 and thymosin beta-4 are not the same substance, and a 2024 lab study found TB-500 itself had no wound-healing effect.

evidence.why: There are no human studies; the evidence is animal and lab work, mostly on the full thymosin beta-4 protein or related peptides, and a lab test of TB-500 itself found no wound-healing effect.

status_us.label: Not approved; compounding not yet allowed
status_us.note: FDA took TB-500 off its Category 2 safety-risk list in April 2026; in July 2026 its advisory committee voted 8-6 (1 abstention) to recommend allowing compounding for wound healing, although FDA staff had proposed not adding it. As of mid-October 2026 FDA had not added it to the compounding list or issued an interim policy, so compounding was still not permitted.

benefits.claim: Faster skin-wound closure and more collagen in aged mice treated with thymosin beta-4 or a non-acetylated peptide with the same LKKTETQ sequence
The LKKTETQ sequence has been reported to stimulate new blood vessel growth in lab studies
One TB-500 breakdown product caused a small but significant wound closure in a lab-dish test, although TB-500 itself did not

risks.risk: No human safety data: FDA found no clinical studies, case reports or other human exposure data by any route
Immune reactions to the injected peptide, possibly worsened by clumping and impurities
No animal toxicology or cancer studies to judge longer-term safety
A report to FDA of skin and gum darkening, which returned on re-use, after injections of a product blending TB-500 with BPC-157; cause not established

avoid_if: Pregnant or breastfeeding (not studied in people)
Current or past cancer, unless a clinician advises otherwise (linked to blood vessel growth in lab work; no cancer studies)
Athletes subject to anti-doping rules (TB-500 is banned by WADA)

before: General health check (complete blood count and metabolic panel) if a clinician is involved
labs.why: TB-500 has not been studied in people, so no evidence-based monitoring exists.

studies.title: FDA Briefing Document for TB-500-Related Bulk Drug Substances (TB-500 (free base) and TB-500 acetate)
studies.people: All published studies; no human studies found
studies.finding: FDA found no human studies, case reports or toxicology studies of TB-500 and proposed not adding it to the compounding list. It noted no TB-500 products are authorized in the EU, Canada, Australia or the UK.

studies.title: Simultaneous Quantification of TB-500 and Its Metabolites in In-Vitro Experiments and Rats
studies.people: Fibroblasts (connective-tissue cells) in a lab-dish scratch test, plus rats
studies.finding: TB-500 showed no wound-healing effect in the scratch test; one of its breakdown products caused a small closure. Findings as summarized by FDA.

studies.title: Thymosin β4 and a synthetic peptide containing its actin-binding domain promote dermal wound repair in db/db diabetic mice and in aged mice
studies.finding: Thymosin beta-4 and a non-acetylated LKKTETQ peptide applied to wounds increased wound closure and collagen in aged mice. Findings as summarized by FDA, which urged caution in interpreting them.

ask_your_clinician: Is there any human evidence for TB-500, as opposed to the full thymosin beta-4 protein?

notes_for_editor: The seed record conflated TB-500 with full-length thymosin beta-4 (its 'limited' grade and trial list came from the full protein's eye-drop and gel trials). FDA's 2026 review says they are not the same substance and found no human data for TB-500, so the grade is now 'preclinical'; full-protein trials belong in the separate tb4 entry. The two animal and lab studies are cited through FDA's summary, not opened directly (our search budget ran out). Status is moving: an HHS/FDA interim access policy for some peptides went to the White House on October 14, 2026 and had not been issued as of October 16 [4]; re-check before publishing. WADA source [6] backs the anti-doping line. FDA's adverse-event summary names the seller of the blended product; omitted on purpose.
